display_fill_tip:
Paint the inside of each circle with the rule colour.
Turn it off to see only the outline.
display_show_names_tip: Write the rule name beside each circle (the effect's type id when the rule has no name).
display_outline_width_tip:
Thickness of the circle outline.
A thin dark edge is drawn under it so it stays visible on bright ground.
display_opacity_tip:
Fades every circle and name together.
Each rule's own colour keeps its transparency on top of this.
display_smoothness_tip:
Points per circle.
More points look rounder and cost a little more time each frame.
display_height_offset_tip:
Moves every circle up or down in the world (negative values lift it).
Leave it at 0 unless circles float above or sink into the ground.
visibility_hostile_tip:
Skip ground effects your side created (your own and your allies' skills).
Effects whose side cannot be read are skipped too.
visibility_town_tip: Draw nothing in towns and hideouts, where ground effects are harmless.
visibility_foreground: Only while the game window is active
visibility_foreground_tip: Hide the circles while another window (a browser, the desktop) is in front of the game.
visibility_hide_menu: Hide while the POEFixer menu is open
visibility_hide_menu_tip:
Hide the circles while the POEFixer menu is shown.
Leave it off to see colour changes live while you edit the rules.
rules_on_tip: Use this rule. A switched-off rule keeps its settings.
rules_colour_tip:
Circle colour.
Its transparency is the fill strength; the outline is drawn stronger.
rules_name_tip: Name shown beside the circle when "{option}" is on.
rules_match_tip:
Text to look for in the effect's type id, visuals and path (not case-sensitive).
Example: ShockedGround, IgnitedGround, CausticCloud.
rules_up_tip:
Move up.
Rules are tried from the top; the first match wins.
rules_help:
Each rule colours the ground effects whose type id, visuals or path contain its match text, for example ShockedGround.

Rules are tried from the top and the first enabled match wins, so put specific rules above general ones.

To find the type id of an effect you see in game, open Diagnostics below and turn on "{option}".
rules_none: No rules: nothing is marked. Add a rule or restore the defaults.
rules_add_tip:
Add an empty rule at the bottom.
Type a match text to make it work.
rules_restore_tip: Replace all rules with the four default ones (shocked, chilled and ignited ground, caustic clouds).
rules_restore_confirm: Replace all rules with the four default rules? Your own rules are removed.
perf_interval_tip:
How often the plugin looks for ground effects that appeared.
Circles already shown follow the camera every frame either way.
perf_budget_tip:
The most time one frame may spend looking.
A longer search continues in the next frames, so the game never stutters.
A scan normally needs far less than 1 ms.
perf_max_circles_tip: Upper limit of circles drawn at the same time.
discovery_nothing_yet: Nothing seen yet. Walk near a ground effect in a map.
discovery_turn_on: Turn on "{option}" to list the ground effects around you.
discovery_add_rule_tip: Add a rule for this type id at the bottom of the rule list.
diag_tip: Scan counts, the path filter and a list of the ground effects around you with their type ids.
diag_marked_now: Marked now: {marked}. Drawn this frame: {drawn} ({ms} ms).
diag_last_scan: Last scan: {entities} entities, {reads} component reads, {ms} ms over {frames} frame(s).
diag_prefilter_tip:
Read only entities whose metadata path looks like a ground effect.
Turn it off only if an effect you see in game never shows up in the discovery list.
diag_discover_tip:
List every kind of ground effect near you this session, with its type id.
Use it to write rules for effects the defaults do not cover.
Not saved: it is off again next time.
diag_write_log_tip: Append each newly seen kind once to config/GroundEffectsDiscovery.log in the plugin folder.
diag_clear_list_tip:
Empty the discovery list.
Effects still around are listed again.
host_too_old: This POEFixer version is too old for Ground Effects: nothing is drawn. Update POEFixer to use the plugin.
